The controls need to be re done. Crafting is confusing and interacting with items is clunky. While the dice are cool, its just annoying to play this game in its current state and please for the love of god let me save my game. Also, the tutorial does a good job of showing you [i]how[/i] to play the game, it just leaves you lost. I played this game because gambling funny haha, but rolling the dice either gives you a neutral outcome (basic resources to play the game), or a bad outcome (seagulls, crabs, ect.). I say bad because its just more work for those essential resources. I would love to see dice outcomes that are more positive to get that gambling buzz, instead of "oh, i guess i'll need that later", which is about as exciting as the dice rolling gets. Don't get me wrong, there are some good bones in this game, but i simply cannot recommend it nor have fun playing it right now. 1/10

Let me guess — you missed the seagull. Again. And instead of accepting that your aim is as useful as a wet matchstick, you came here to leave a bad review tantrum? This game doesn’t hold your hand. It doesn’t even know what a hand is. It hands you a hammer, a pile of parts, and a look that says “figure it out.” And I respect that. Crafting with real-time hammer swings? That’s not a QTE, that’s a mini-career. The seagulls? You have to lead your shots. Wind, angle, beak patterns — this is sniper-level poultry combat. And when you do hit one, oh man. Pure dopamine. Skill > spray-and-pray. Dice rolls? It’s not just luck. You’ve got to time them. That’s right — even RNG bows to rhythm here. Think you’re unlucky? You’re probably just bad at counting. And don’t even get me started on the snakes, eels, and turtles. That ecosystem is like a slippery, bitey chessboard. Misstep once, and a turtle’s wearing your spleen as a hat. So yeah, this game’s hard. That’s the point. It's not broken, you are. If you're the type to ragequit because the game didn't give you a participation trophy, go back to Candy Crush. The rest of us will be over here, hammering out armor, timing our rolls, and picking feathers out of our teeth.

It's not a virus, but it sure feels like unfinished slop. Played it with a friend for like 5 rounds and saw labout everything you need to see in about an hour. There are few things I've got to say about this game: - Controls are whacky! You pick up things with left mouse button, use them with the same button, discard them with the right button and eat them with q. To me it feels like something you should get used to, even though it's the only game that does that. - you get achievements after closing the game. in my case, i got 30 popups just by playing for an hour. that feels a lil unprofessional - hammers should not be obtainable through a dice. you need them asap, and you shouldn't get them by throwing dices. it is more likely to get killed by snakes or crabs. - the tutorial was to vague. barely anything is explained, not even the fact that you can summon bosses by throwing dices! - too little food and too many enemies. balance it out! - no save option but at least 5 bosses for which you come unprepared and as I said, once in a while you can get them while you are trying to gamble for food. - why is there an option to make a private lobby? I thought these were for friends but no.friend lobbies have their own options.

Is it fun? Sure, for a bit. Will I try to 100% it? Yeah, because I hate myself. Is it good? No. The crafting system makes no sense. Not only the menus, but the fact that you have to roll the dice to even unlock the item to allow you to craft. Either you or the enemies are constantly kicking around items all over the place so you're always losing track of things, like your weapons. For the crafting items you kick around, if they aren't in the same general area, it won't let you craft. You cannot save the game and continue. If you die, you have to start over (this wouldn't be an issue but the game never advertises itself as a rogue-like or rogue-lite). The D20 never wants to stop rolling towards the water, so you find yourself waiting longer than you would expect to get your dice back. Again, not necessarily a big problem until you realize early your only weapon are the dice, and you are not allowed to pick them back up until they finish rolling (and throwing them at enemies counts as a roll).

"Pair A Dice" is a badly made low poly dice-centric RPG-lite that has you do some boss fights and RPG fights by rolling dice... it's not a great idea even if implemented well, and this has a very poor quality delivery. Content is locked behind DLC, you have to pay five bucks to unlock the full game, as the developer sought to mislead gamers with deceptive pricing and abusing the free section of Steam with a non-free game. Despite not being in Early Access, it's obvious this is an incomplete product. Developers have an obligation to deliver complete, not partially done products to gamers, that shouldn't be controversial. Whatever the excuses may be, it does no service to gamers for incomplete products polluting Steam like this. It makes it harder for gamers to find complete games, and it makes it harder for ethical developers who do the right thing to find their audience. In terms of visuals, this features fairly low quality low poly 3D graphics which will deter a lot of gamers, understandably. Gaming is a visual medium, and while some developers struggle with creating high quality visuals, failing to do so is a disservice to gamers. It's very difficult to recommend bad looking games. The developer chose not to do the job of a real game developer and create meaningful bespoke levels, narrative based gameplay progression and so on. Instead, they decided that "Procgen IS content!" and lazily tried to use procgen algorithms to create infinite, samey, repetitive, soulless levels, because that's a lot less work. As a result of this poor decision, the game gets tired and repetitive almost immediately. Developers must learn that procgen is a terrible substitute for creating real content. It should not be used as "ez-mode" for content creation, as the developer tried to do here. Now on to pricing and value for gamers. You're expected to pay up $5 USD to unlock content through DLC purchases. The game should not be considered completely unlocked until you empty your wallet for the developer. This is misleading and predatory pricing on a product falsely marketed as "free". It's important to note that, despite this being such a low quality product, there's a number of positive reviews that all appeared immediately after the game launched, from suspiciously inactive Steam accounts that have reviewed almost no other games apart from this. Take the review score of this game with a grain of salt. Given that this free title won't increase your game collector count, is it worth your time to add it to your library? Definitely not. This isn't worth it. I'm paraphrasing another reviewer here, but this should be a paid product... they'd have to pay people to download it.
